headline: Stripe vs PayPal Fees in 2026
description: Compare typical US online Stripe (2.9%+$0.30) and PayPal Goods & Services (3.49%+$0.49) fees, $100 examples, FX notes, and when each processor wins.

mainEntity.name: Is Stripe always cheaper than PayPal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. On common US online list rates, Stripe’s 2.9% + $0.30 beats PayPal G&S 3.49% + $0.49 on a like-for-like card charge, but custom pricing, regions, international cards, and product mix can flip the result. Compare with your average order value in /tools/compare-payment-fees/.

mainEntity.name: Can I offer both Stripe and PayPal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many stores offer Stripe (cards) and PayPal as a wallet option. Track the effective blended fee in your books and make sure reverse-priced catalog prices still clear your net target on the more expensive rail you accept.

mainEntity.name: Does PayPal Friends & Family change the comparison?

acceptedAnswer.text: F&F can be $0 for eligible personal payments from balance or bank, but it is the wrong tool for selling goods and services to customers. Commercial sales should use Goods & Services (or another merchant product) despite the higher fee.

mainEntity.name: How big is the gap on $100?

acceptedAnswer.text: About $0.78 in fees on a $100 charge using the US list schedules above (Stripe $3.20 vs PayPal G&S ~$3.98). At volume that gap compounds; at tiny volume conversion differences may matter more than $0.78.

mainEntity.name: What about Square or Shopify Payments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Square online and Shopify Payments Basic also list 2.9% + $0.30 for common online US card pricing, similar to Stripe’s headline shape. For a three-way commerce comparison, read Square vs Stripe vs Shopify Payments.
